info.title: Tassyir developer API
info.summary: The API a developer calls to build Tassyir apps: their account, apps, client secrets, versions, marketplace listings, the webhook console, dev stores and the CLI sign-in.
info.description:
The routes under `/developer/` that a DEVELOPER calls: the developer console, the `tassyir` CLI and the dev MCP. Not an app's API: installed apps call the Admin API, which has its own document. Guides: https://developers.tassyir.io.

**Authentication.** `Authorization: Bearer <dashboard JWT>` (the console) or `Authorization: Bearer tsy_dt_…` (a developer token from the CLI sign-in), on every route but the approval routes (the dashboard session only) and the two public RFC 8628 routes. A developer account belongs to a USER, not a business: no route takes a business id, and an id that is not yours answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist.

**Conventions.** JSON fields are camelCase (snake_case on the two OAuth routes, as RFC 8628 has them); ids are strings; times are ISO 8601 UTC. One resource answers `{ data }`, a paged list `{ data, nextCursor }` (pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`), a short list `{ data }`.

**Errors.** Not problem+json: the dashboard API's shape. A coded refusal is `{ statusCode, code, message, fix?, …subject, requestId }` (`DeveloperError`); act on `code`. Three refusals carry no `code` today: a request that fails validation (400, `message` is a list of sentences), a missing or ended dashboard session (401), and the platform-wide rate limit (429, a bare JSON string). The two OAuth routes answer `{ error, error_description }`. Each operation lists every code it can answer, by status.

**Limits.** Each developer has caps (apps, secrets, versions, dev stores), and the console's replays and tests and the CLI sign-in have rate limits of their own, which apply whether or not the platform-wide rate limit is enforced; each operation says which apply.

post.summary: Mint a client secret (the first, or a rotation)
post.description:
The secret is in this answer ONCE. Minting while other secrets are live is the rotation: each live secret with no end date gets `expiresAt = now + 24 h`. At most 3 live secrets per app; 10 minted per developer per hour. No body.

Takes the dashboard session or a developer token (`tsy_dt_…`); either way the caller is the signed-in user, and only their own account, apps and tokens are reachable.

The whole draft: a field you leave out (or send `null`) is cleared. Every rule is checked at once (`LISTING_INVALID` lists each problem with its `path`); an incomplete draft is saved and its gaps come back as `issues`. Plain text only: no HTML, no Markdown links, no invisible characters. The draft never reaches the marketplace by itself: Tassyir reviews it first.

post.description:
One image a call, as `multipart/form-data`: the file in `file`, its `kind`. The BYTES decide what it is: PNG, JPEG or WebP (never SVG or GIF), at most 2 MB. An icon is square, 512 to 1200 px; a desktop screenshot 16:9 from 1600x900 to 3200x1800; a mobile one 9:16 from 900x1600 to 1800x3200. An app holds at most 20 images (drafts included), and a developer uploads at most 30 every 10 minutes. An image no draft names is deleted 7 days after it was uploaded.

Takes the dashboard session or a developer token (`tsy_dt_…`); either way the caller is the signed-in user, and only their own account, apps and tokens are reachable.

post.summary: Upload a version of the app's manifest
post.description:
The body is at most 128 KB (8 MB + 128 KB while Tassyir Hosting is on) and nests at most 16 levels (its own parser); a larger body is 413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` with `limitBytes`, `hostingAvailable` and a `fix` saying why (while hosting is off, only a version carrying a bundle is that large). The validator checks the manifest (every error at once); `handle` must be the app's; a manifest identical to the latest version's (and, hosted, the same bundle) is refused. An external version is numbered latest + 1, approved and current at once, except for a LISTED app: there it must subscribe the three compliance topics and name a supported API version (400 `REVIEW_CHECKS_FAILED`, nothing stored), and a version that adds scopes, data hosts or storefront code waits `in_review` for a person (a `version` review case opens by itself). A hosted version (`hosting.mode = "tassyir"`, while Tassyir Hosting is on and open to your developer account) carries its `bundle`, stored before the version is created `scanning`; it is scanned, uploaded and released by the hosting pipeline. 30 uploads per developer per hour, 10 hosted a day.

Takes the dashboard session or a developer token (`tsy_dt_…`); either way the caller is the signed-in user, and only their own account, apps and tokens are reachable.

Print `user_code`, open `verification_uri_complete` (it only pre-fills the code: the developer approves on the page, signed in to the dashboard), then poll `POST /developer/cli/token` every `interval` seconds. 10 sign-ins per IP every 10 minutes. Errors are OAuth's `{ error, error_description }`.

Public: the CLI holds nothing yet.

post.description:
The approval page's route (dashboard JWT ONLY: a developer token can never approve a sign-in). The code travels in the body; dashes, spaces and case are ignored. An unknown, expired or someone else's code is one answer, 404 `CLI_CODE_NOT_FOUND`. 10 approvals per user an hour; 10 wrong codes per user and 30 per IP an hour. Only on the developer's click, never automatically. Idempotent. The CLI's next poll receives the token, and the developer is told (a bell notification and a push).

Takes the dashboard session ONLY: a developer token is refused here, so a stolen CLI token can never approve a new sign-in.

post.description:
Every `interval` seconds: `authorization_pending` until the developer decides; `slow_down` (HTTP 400) when a poll comes too soon, after which the interval is 5 seconds longer (at most 60); stop on `access_denied`, `expired_token` or `invalid_grant`. A device code yields one token, once. 30 unknown device codes per IP a minute (429 `slow_down`).

Public: the CLI holds nothing yet.
